inclusion_rule: Models that map a non-acoustic speech signal (ultrasound, EMA or PMA, EMG, lip video, other wearable sensors) to speech, text or articulatory output and adapt a trained model to a new speaker or recording session with target data, reporting an unadapted or full-retraining comparison; classified by what is adapted (whole network, a layer subset, an input-space transform, or an input prompt/padding/embedding). Boundary: acoustic-only systems, speaker-independent training without an adaptation step, neural-recording calibration, tongue-contour tracking and reviews are excluded; versions counted once.

usual_approach.design: feature- or model-space linear transforms (fMLLR, MLLR, Procrustes) in recognizers, or weight updates on target data (whole network or a layer subset) and speaker inputs (i-vector, padding, prompts) in neural models; no learned image-space transform before the target
usual_approach.note: full-text pattern counts over the 93 unique candidate studies (reference lists removed; a study can match several): input-space or feature-space transform 17, speaker prompt/padding/embedding 10, layer-subset update 5, domain-adversarial 5, whole-network fine-tuning wording 3. A spatial-transformer or learned image-affine hit outside the target's own three versions occurs only in a [later] survey (arxiv-2603.11877) that cites the target and in a lip-to-speech Transformer naming (arxiv-2207.03800, not an adaptation module); affine hits elsewhere are fixed face alignment (arxiv-2502.05758) or MLLR/fMLLR on model or feature space (isca-hueber13b_interspeech, isca-beeson23_interspeech). Ultrasound session adaptation before the target: doi-10.12700-aph.17.7.2020.7.6 (lower-layer weight update). Slot-filled M03 values (supervision_kind) do not describe the adaptation design.

read_fulltext.quote: we extend our deep networks with a spatial transformer network (STN) module
adapting just the lower, feature extractor layers of the neural network proved to be sufficient
until now there have been no methods yet for auto-rotating within longer ultrasound recording sessions
adapting on 5 minutes video achieves 5.67% WER
The proposed method achieves a marginally higher WER of 40.9%
